correctness.rationale: For every bounded symplectic congruence S, the Hamiltonian T=J(A+B) is similar to the normal Hamiltonian J(D⊕D). Polynomial/holomorphic functional calculus yields ||T(-T²+εI)^(-1/2)||≤||S||||S^-1||. Direct block multiplication computes this norm as ess sup max(cp,cq)/sqrt(c²pq+ε); monotone limit is sqrt R even if c²pq approaches zero. A reciprocal fourth-root multiplier S is bounded, symplectic, simultaneous, and attains sqrt R precisely for finite R. The example p=1,q=t²,a=t,b=1-t satisfies all hypotheses, R=∞. The finite code is only a sanity test, not an infinite proof.
